{{Short description|ISO standard for country codes}}
'''ISO 3166-1''' (''Codes for the representation of names of countries and their subdivisions &ndash; Part 1: Country code'') is a standard defining codes for the names of countries, dependent territories, and special areas of geographical interest. It is the first part of the [[ISO 3166]] [[Standardization|standard]] published by the [[International Organization for Standardization]].

It defines three sets of [[country code]]s:<ref name="iso3166-info">{{cite web| url=https://www.iso.org/iso-3166-country-codes.html| title=Country Codes – ISO 3166| publisher=International Organization for Standardization (ISO)| access-date=2018-05-09| archive-date=2017-01-23| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170123191048/http://www.iso.org/iso/iso-3166-1_decoding_table| url-status=live}}</ref>
* [[ISO 3166-1 alpha-2]] – two-letter country codes which are used most prominently for the Internet's [[country code top-level domain]]s (with a few exceptions).
* [[ISO 3166-1 alpha-3]] – three-letter country codes which allow a better visual association between the codes and the country names than the alpha-2 codes.
* [[ISO 3166-1 numeric]] – three-digit country codes which are identical to those developed and maintained by the [[United Nations Statistics Division]], with the advantage of script ([[writing system]]) independence, and hence useful for people or systems using non-[[Latin alphabet|Latin]] scripts.

The alphabetic country codes were first included in ISO 3166 in 1974, and the numeric country codes were first included in 1981. The country codes have been published as ISO 3166-1 since 1997, when ISO 3166 was expanded into three parts, with [[ISO 3166-2]] defining codes for [[Administrative division|subdivisions]] and [[ISO 3166-3]] defining codes for [[List of former sovereign states|former countries]].<ref name="iso3166-info">{{cite web| url=https://www.iso.org/iso-3166-country-codes.html| title=Country Codes – ISO 3166| publisher=International Organization for Standardization (ISO)| access-date=2018-05-09| archive-date=2017-01-23| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170123191048/http://www.iso.org/iso/iso-3166-1_decoding_table| url-status=live}}</ref>

As a widely used international standard, ISO 3166-1 is implemented in other standards and used by [[international organization]]s<ref name="iso3166-info"/> to allow facilitation of the exchange of goods and information.<ref name="iso3166-info"/> However, it is not the only standard for country codes. [[Country code#Other country codes|Other country codes]] used by many international organizations are partly or totally incompatible with ISO 3166-1,<ref name="iso3166-info"/> although some of them closely correspond to ISO 3166-1 codes.

==Criteria for inclusion==

Codes for 249 countries, territories, or areas of geographical interest are assigned in ISO 3166-1.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.iso.org/obp/ui/#search/code/| title=Country names and code elements| publisher=ISO| quote=Officially assigned codes 249| access-date=2020-09-07| archive-date=2016-06-17| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160617031837/https://www.iso.org/obp/ui/#search/code/| url-status=live}}</ref> According to the ISO 3166 Maintenance Agency (ISO 3166/MA), the only way to enter a new country name into ISO 3166-1 is to have it registered in one of the following two sources:<ref name="iso3166-info"/>
* United Nations Terminology Bulletin ''Country Names'', or
* ''Country and Region Codes for Statistical Use'' of the [[United Nations Statistics Division]].

To be listed in the bulletin ''Country Names'', a country must be at least one of the following:<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.iana.org/help/eligible-tlds| title=Qualifying top-level domain strings: Eligible categories of top-level domains| publisher=Internet Assigned Numbers Authority| access-date=2014-02-25| archive-date=2014-02-28| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140228181535/https://www.iana.org/help/eligible-tlds| url-status=live}}</ref>

* A [[Member states of the United Nations|member state of the United Nations]]
* A member of one of its [[List of specialized agencies of the United Nations|specialized agencies]]
* A party to the ''[[Statute of the International Court of Justice]]''

The list of names in ''Country and Region Codes for Statistical Use'' of the UN Statistics Division is based on the bulletin ''Country Names'' and other UN sources.

Once a country name or territory name appears in either of these two sources, it will be added to ISO 3166-1 by default.

The ISO 3166/MA may [[#Reserved and user-assigned code elements|reserve code elements]] for other entities that do not qualify for inclusion based on the above criteria.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.iso.org/iso/en/prods-services/iso3166ma/10faq/frequently-asked-questions.html#Q07| title=ISO 3166 &ndash; FAQs &ndash; General Questions| date=29 September 2006| publisher=ISO |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070306080355/http://www.iso.org/iso/en/prods-services/iso3166ma/10faq/frequently-asked-questions.html#Q07 |archive-date=2007-03-06}}</ref> For example, because the [[European Union]] is not a country, it is not formally included in ISO 3166-1, but for practical reasons, the ISO 3166/MA has "reserved the two-letter combination {{mono|EU}} for the purpose of identifying the European Union within the framework of ISO 3166-1".<ref name="faqs_specific">{{cite web| url=http://www.iso.org/iso/country_codes/iso_3166-faqs/iso_3166_faqs_specific.htm| title=ISO 3166 &ndash; FAQs &ndash; Specific| publisher=ISO |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120616044022/http://www.iso.org/iso/country_codes/iso_3166-faqs/iso_3166_faqs_specific.htm |archive-date=2012-06-16}}</ref>

==Information included==

ISO 3166-1 is published officially in both [[English language|English]] and [[French language|French]]. Since the second edition of ISO 3166-1, the following columns are included for each entry:
# Country Name&nbsp;– English (or French) short name (all upper-case)
# English (or French) [[List of ISO 3166 country codes|short name lower case]] (title case)
# English (or French) full name
# [[ISO 3166-1 alpha-2|Alpha-2 code]]
# [[ISO 3166-1 alpha-3|Alpha-3 code]]
# [[ISO 3166-1 numeric|Numeric code]]
# Remarks
# Independent
# Additional information: [[Official language|Administrative language(s)]] [[ISO 639-1|alpha-2 code element(s)]]
# Additional information: Administrative language(s) [[ISO 639-2|alpha-3 code element(s)]]
# Additional information: [[List of countries by native names|Local short name(s)]]

===Coding===

The codes are chosen, according to the ISO 3166/MA, "to reflect the significant, unique component of the country name in order to allow a visual association between country name and country code".<ref name="faqs_specific" /> For this reason, common components of country names like "Republic", "Kingdom", "United", "Federal" or "Democratic" are normally not used for deriving the code elements. As a consequence, for example, the [[United Kingdom]] is officially assigned the alpha-2 code {{mono|GB}} rather than {{mono|UK}}, based on its official name "United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland" (although {{mono|UK}} is [[#Reserved and user-assigned code elements|reserved]] on the request of the United Kingdom). The rule is not watertight: the [[United States of America]] is still assigned the {{mono|US}} code for example. Some codes are chosen based on the native names of the countries. For example, Germany is assigned the alpha-2 code {{mono|DE}}, based on its native name "Deutschland".

===Reserved and user-assigned code elements===
The officially assigned code elements may be expanded by using either reserved codes or user-assigned codes.<ref name="iso3166-info"/>

Reserved code elements are codes which have become obsolete, are used in other coding systems such as [[WIPO ST.3]], or are required in order to enable a particular user application of the standard but do not qualify for inclusion in ISO 3166-1. To avoid transitional application problems and to aid users who require specific additional code elements for the functioning of their coding systems, the ISO 3166/MA, when justified, reserves these codes for a certain use for a limited or indeterminate period of time. Codes are usually reserved for former countries, overseas territories, international organizations, and special nationality status. The reserved alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes can be divided into three categories:<br>
''(follow the links for the reserved codes of each category)''
* [[ISO 3166-1 alpha-2#Reserved code elements|Alpha-2]]: [[ISO 3166-1 alpha-2#Exceptional reservations|exceptional reservations]], [[ISO 3166-1 alpha-2#Transitional reservations|transitional reservations]], and [[ISO 3166-1 alpha-2#Indeterminate reservations|indeterminate reservations]]
* [[ISO 3166-1 alpha-3#Reserved code elements|Alpha-3]]: [[ISO 3166-1 alpha-3#Exceptional reservations|exceptional reservations]], [[ISO 3166-1 alpha-3#Transitional reservations|transitional reservations]], and [[ISO 3166-1 alpha-3#Indeterminate reservations|indeterminate reservations]]
* Numeric: no reserved codes

User-assigned code elements are codes at the disposal of users who need to add further names of countries, territories, or other geographical entities to their in-house application of ISO 3166-1, and the ISO 3166/MA will never use these codes when updating the standard. These codes can be user-assigned:<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.iso.org/glossary-for-iso-3166.html| title=Glossary for ISO 3166 - Codes for countries and their subdivisions| publisher=ISO| access-date=2018-11-13| archive-date=2018-07-28| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180728035756/https://www.iso.org/glossary-for-iso-3166.html| url-status=live}}</ref>
* [[ISO 3166-1 alpha-2#User-assigned code elements|Alpha-2]]: {{mono|AA}}, {{mono|QM}} to {{mono|QZ}}, {{mono|XA}} to {{mono|XZ}}, and {{mono|ZZ}}
* [[ISO 3166-1 alpha-3#User-assigned code elements|Alpha-3]]: {{mono|AAA}} to {{mono|AAZ}}, {{mono|QMA}} to {{mono|QZZ}}, {{mono|XAA}} to {{mono|XZZ}}, and {{mono|ZZA}} to {{mono|ZZZ}}
* [[ISO 3166-1 numeric#User-assigned code elements|Numeric]]: {{mono|900}} to {{mono|999}}

====User-assigned codes in wide use====
{{further|ISO 3166-1 alpha-2#User-assigned code elements|ISO 3166-1 alpha-3#User-assigned code elements|ISO 3166-1 numeric#User-assigned code elements}}
* {{mono|XI}}: Used to denote [[Northern Ireland]] for the purposes of [[Value-added tax|VAT]] collection in trade between it and the [[European Union]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/accounting-for-vat-on-goods-moving-between-great-britain-and-northern-ireland-from-1-january-2021/check-when-you-are-trading-under-the-northern-ireland-protocol-if-you-are-vat-registered-business | title=Check if you're trading under the Northern Ireland protocol and what to do | date=2020-12-07 | access-date=2021-01-08 | publisher=HM Revenue & Customs, UK | archive-date=2021-01-09 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210109220340/https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/accounting-for-vat-on-goods-moving-between-great-britain-and-northern-ireland-from-1-january-2021/check-when-you-are-trading-under-the-northern-ireland-protocol-if-you-are-vat-registered-business | url-status=live }}</ref>
* {{mono|XK}}: Used to denote [[Kosovo]]- see [[XK (user assigned code)]].

==Changes==

The ISO 3166/MA updates ISO 3166-1 when necessary. A country is normally assigned new ISO 3166-1 codes if it changes its name or its territorial boundaries. In general, new alphabetic codes are assigned if a country changes a significant part of its name, while a new numeric code is assigned if a country changes its territorial boundaries. Codes for country names that have been deleted from ISO 3166-1 are published in [[ISO 3166-3]].

ISO formerly announced changes in newsletters which updated the standard, and periodically released new editions which consolidated the newsletter changes. As of July 2013, changes are published in the online catalogue of ISO only, and newsletters are no longer published. Past newsletters remain available via the search option on the ISO website.<ref name="Updates on ISO 3166">{{cite web| url=https://www.iso.org/iso-3166-1-new-access.html| title=ISO 3166-1 - New access| publisher=ISO| access-date=2017-07-19| archive-date=2021-05-09| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210509094130/https://www.iso.org/iso-3166-country-codes.html| url-status=live}}</ref>
